blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Benchmark compression reduces evaluation cost by selecting a small set of samples. Existing methods typically guide selection using a single metric, although benchmarks often assess models along multiple dimensions. We find that model rankings are often weakly correlated across metrics, indicating that different metrics capture distinct aspects of model performance. Samples selected for one metric do not reliably preserve scores and rankings on others when used for compressed evaluation. At 80\% compression, each of the five single-metric baselines yields higher reconstruction error than equal-size random sampling in over 70\% of cross-metric comparisons. To address this challenge, we present HoloCosm, which jointly minimizes normalized score-reconstruction error across source models and metrics while constraining ranking distortion. We evaluate HoloCosm across multiple compression rates on 15 language, multimodal, VLA, and agent benchmark configurations with 85 component metrics. With 80\% compression, HoloCosm outperforms Random, the strongest baseline overall: average NMAE drops by 35.3\% to 0.236, worst-component NMAE drops by 39.5\% to 0.330, and average Spearman correlation rises from 0.884 to 0.915. In addition, HoloCosm remains competitive with existing baselines in single-metric evaluation. We will release our code and experimental results.
blocks.zh: 基准压缩通过选择一小组样本来降低评价成本. 现行方法通常使用单一的衡量标准来指导选择,尽管基准往往按照多个层面评估模型。 我们发现,模型排名在各种衡量尺度之间往往互不关联,这表明不同的衡量尺度捕捉模型业绩的不同方面。 为一个衡量标准选择的样本在用于压缩评价时,不能可靠地保持分数和对其他分数的排名。 在80+Q压缩时,在70+Q的交叉测量比较中,5个单量基线中的每个都产生比等大小随机抽样更高的重建出错. 为了应对这一挑战,我们提出HoloCosm,它共同将源模型和度量衡之间正常的分数重建错误降到最低,同时限制排名扭曲。 我们评价HoloCosm在15种语言、多模式、VLA和具有85个组件度量的代理基准配置上的多重压缩率。 80\%压缩后,"HoloCosm"超越了性能"随机",是总体最强的基准:NMAE平均下降35.3\%到0.236;最差组件NMAE下降39.5\%到0.330;平均斯皮尔曼相关从0.884到0.915. 此外,HoloCosm在单计量评价中仍然与现有基线有竞争力。 我们将发布我们的代码和实验结果。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: As the number of models and the scale of evaluation continue to grow, repeatedly evaluating models on full benchmarks incurs increasing computational and time costs. Benchmark compression reduces this burden by selecting a small set of representative samples to approximate full-benchmark model scores and rankings. Existing benchmark compression methods ( BCMs ), such as AnchorPoints, tinyBenchmarks, mRMR-based compression, SubLIME, and ZipBench, aim to substantially reduce benchmark size while maintaining high evaluation fidelity through representative sample selection for downstream model comparison ( Vivek et al., 2024 ; Maia Polo et al., 2024 ; Bowyer et al., 2026 ; Saranathan et al., 2025 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) . However, these methods typically guide sample selection using a single evaluation metric, whereas modern benchmarks often assess models along multiple dimensions. This exposes a key issue: samples considered representative under one metric may not be equally representative for other metrics.
blocks.zh: 随着模型数量和评价规模的继续增加,按全部基准反复评价模型的计算和时间成本增加。 基准压缩通过选择一小组代表性标本来近似全基准模型分数和排名来减轻这一负担. 现有的基准压缩方法(业连管),如AnchorPoints、微小的奔驰、基于mRMR的压缩、SubLIME和Zip Bench,旨在通过选择具有代表性的样本来进行下游模型比较,大幅度缩小基准大小,同时保持高评价的忠实性(Vivek等人,2024年;Maia) Polo等人,2024年;Bowyer等人,2026年;Saranathan等人,2025年;Huang等人,2026年。 然而,这些方法通常使用单一的评价衡量标准指导抽样选择,而现代基准往往按照多个层面评估模型。 这暴露出一个关键问题:一个衡量标准下的样本被认为具有代表性,而其他衡量标准可能不具有同等代表性。

blocks.en: We therefore examine the consistency of model rankings across evaluation metrics. Across 85 official metrics from 15 benchmark configurations spanning language, multimodal, VLA, and agent tasks, we compute Spearman correlations between metric-induced model rankings within each benchmark. As shown in Fig. 1 , many metric pairs exhibit weak ranking agreement, with negative correlations appearing across several benchmarks. Using ρ ≥ 0.85 \rho\geq 0.85 as the threshold for high correlation ( Granato, 2014 ) , we find that highly correlated pairs are only a small fraction in many benchmarks: Bench2Drive has only one out of six such pairs, while LiveIdea-Full4 ( Ruan et al., 2026 ) has none. These results show that different metrics capture distinct, sometimes conflicting, model-comparison information, raising a concern for compression guided by a single metric.
blocks.zh: 因此,我们审查各种评价指标的模型排名的一致性。 我们从15个基准组合中计算出85个官方指标,这些基准组合涉及语言、多式联运、VLA和代理任务,我们计算每个基准中由衡量引起的模型排名之间的斯皮尔曼关系。 如图1所示,许多公尺对数的排名一致,在几个基准中出现负相关性。 使用 ^ 0.85\rho\geq 0.85作为高相关性的门槛(Granato,2014年),我们发现高度关联的对子在许多基准中只是一小部分: Beach2Drive在6对这样的配对中只有1对,而LiveIdea-Full4(Ruan等人,2026年)则没有. 这些结果表明,不同的衡量标准捕捉到不同、有时相互矛盾的模型比较信息,引起了对以单一衡量标准为指导进行压缩的关切。

blocks.en: These cross-metric differences raise a question for single-metric compression: can samples selected to represent one metric also preserve the evaluation information captured by others? To examine this question, we select items using one metric and evaluate them on the remaining metrics of the same benchmark, comparing against equal-size Random sampling at 80% compression. As shown in the left panel of Fig. 2 , existing single-metric BCMs perform worse than Random in 70.5%–97.7% of cross-metric score-reconstruction comparisons across five baselines. The right panel further shows that even when the selected samples achieve lower NMAE than Random on the selection metric, this advantage often fails to carry over to other metrics, where reconstruction errors instead exceed those of Random. These results show that a subset representative of one metric does not necessarily preserve the information needed to evaluate others.
blocks.zh: 这些跨度量差异提出了单度量压缩的问题:选取代表一个度量的样本能否也保存其他计量采集的评价信息? 为了研究这个问题,我们用一个衡量标准来选择项目,并用同一个基准的剩余衡量标准来评价它们,比照压缩80%的相同大小的随机抽样。 如图2左面板所示,现有单一计量的业连管在5个基线的交叉计量分数-重建比较中的表现比Random差70.5~97.7%。 正确的面板进一步表明,即使选取的样本在选取度量上取得了比Random更低的NMAE,这种优势也往往未能延续到其他度量衡,而重建错误却超过了Random. 这些结果表明,一个指标的子代表不一定保留评价其他指标所需的信息。

blocks.en:
To address this systematic cross-metric failure, we present HoloCosm, which directly optimizes evaluation fidelity across multiple metrics rather than assuming that items selected for one metric will transfer to others.
Using full-benchmark evaluation results from source models, HoloCosm minimizes normalized score-reconstruction error across models and metrics while constraining ranking distortion.
Size-matched reference selections calibrate the ranking-distortion constraint, a feasibility-first exchange search refines the selected items, and a source-assisted correction estimates full-benchmark scores while preserving within-metric rankings. At 80% compression (20% retention), HoloCosm achieves the best aggregate performance across 15 benchmark configurations and 85 evaluation metrics. Despite being designed for multi-metric evaluation, HoloCosm remains competitive with existing single-metric BCMs in single-metric settings. Our contributions are: • Multi-metric inconsistency. Across 85 official metrics from 15 benchmark configurations, we find widespread weak and negative correlations between metric-induced model rankings, showing that different evaluation dimensions often capture substantially different information across different types of benchmarks. • Systematic cross-metric failure. At 80% compression, existing single-metric BCMs perform worse than Random in 70.5%–97.7% of cross-metric score-reconstruction comparisons, revealing a systematic failure of single-metric-guided compression. To our knowledge, we are the first to systematically study this multi-metric compression problem. • Multi-metric benchmark compression. We introduce HoloCosm to preserve score and ranking fidelity across metrics. It achieves the best overall fidelity across 15 benchmark configurations and 85 metrics at 80% compression while remaining competitive in single-metric evaluation under the same compression setting.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Benchmark compression reduces evaluation cost by estimating full-benchmark
performance from fewer items.
AnchorPoints, mRMR, and ZipBench select
representative items using response correlation, mutual-information-based
feature selection, and synthesized-response representations, respectively ( Vivek et al., 2024 ; Bowyer et al., 2026 ; Huang et al., 2026 ) .
tinyBenchmarks and bias-bounded item selection focus on accurate score
estimation through IRT-based selection and bias-bounded submodular selection ( Maia Polo et al., 2024 ; Zhuang et al., 2025 ) . More specialized benchmark
compression includes MiniLongBench, which learns sample representations and
clusters them to prune redundant long-context samples while preserving model
rankings ( Huang et al., 2025 ) . SubLIME uses predicted rank correlation
to guide subset selection, while EssenceBench combines redundancy-aware
filtering with fitness-based subset search ( Saranathan et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026 ) . Despite these differences,
existing benchmark-compression methods primarily select items for one
evaluation metric at a time. Tab. 1 summarizes
this distinction. Our work instead uses multiple evaluation metrics for item
selection within the same benchmark while preserving both scores and model
rankings.

We evaluate on 15 benchmark configurations with 85 official
component metrics, as summarized in Tab. 2 .

All methods use the same fixed source–target split.

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We uncover a systematic cross-metric failure in benchmark compression:
subsets selected for one metric often perform worse than equal-size random
sampling on others. To address this, HoloCosm minimizes multi-metric
reconstruction error under a ranking-risk constraint. Across 15 benchmark
configurations, HoloCosm improves score and ranking fidelity over Random.
It remains competitive on single-metric benchmarks and transfers from
weaker source models to stronger targets. Benchmark compression for
multi-metric evaluation should preserve fidelity across metrics.
